newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Germany's Villeroy&Boch in Romania deal.
newsitem.headline: Germany's Villeroy&Boch in Romania deal.

text.p: German tableware and bathroom fittings group Villeroy & Boch took a bigger bite of a Romanian producer on Wednesday as part of a bid to return the group to profit in 1997.

Michel Brosset, member of Villeroy's board of directors, said the German group's stake in the local tiles and sanitary equipment maker Mondiala, based in Lugoj, 500 km (300 miles) west of Bucharest, had now reached 95 percent.
Last year Villeroy acquired 51 percent of Mondiala.

Earlier this year, the German group pledged to cut costs by transferring production to cheaper sites like Hungary and Romania and adjusting its portfolio to market demands. Villeroy sustained a net loss of 103 million German marks ($56 million) last year.

Brosset said the group purchased the stake held in Mondiala by Romania's main privatisation agency, the State Ownership Fund (FPS), but gave no details of the value of the deal or Mondiala's share capital. The remaining five percent is held by the company's employees' association.
Villeroy pledged to invest at least 20 million marks over the coming four years. Brosset said his group had already put more than 10 million marks in new buildings and equipment.
He said the company had sold its products both on the Romanian market and in other Eastern European countries.

Mondiala posted a seven billion lei ($970,000) gross profit in 1996, and had a 40 billion lei turnover in the first seven months of 1997, according to its director general Pavel Bidderman. He said the new investment would increase tile production to threefold and double plumbing equipment output.
The factory has an annual capacity of two million square metre of tiles and 500,000 pieces of plumbing equipment.
-- Diana Voicu, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264 ($ = 1.837 German Marks) ($ = 7210 Romanian Lei)
